issues.detail: The code is tied to React/Next.js (App Router, proxy.ts, next/server) and Google Consent Mode, with only brief mention of vanilla JS and no non-Next server equivalents for the consent endpoint or GPC detection.

scenarios.name: nextjs-banner-gated-ga4
scenarios.rationale: Response A sets inline Consent Mode v2 defaults to denied for all four signals in the head, loads gtag.js only after analytics consent through a consent store that sends a 'consent update', and puts Reject all, Accept all and Customize on the first layer with identical styling; Response B has no Consent Mode defaults and no Customize option, and only gates the script on a localStorage flag with plain Accept and Reject buttons.

scenarios.name: gpc-signal-server-and-client
scenarios.rationale: B covers all three rubric items (client-side GPC check saving a 'gpc' rejection without the banner, proxy.ts setting a gpc_optout cookie, and a curl -sI -H 'Sec-GPC: 1' test for the cookie), while A never sets a gpc_optout cookie, never saves consent with source 'gpc', and its curl test greps page HTML instead of checking a cookie.

scenarios.name: consent-withdrawal-and-versioned-records
scenarios.rationale: Response B covers nearly every rubric element (record with version, timestamp, preferences and source, CONSENT_VERSION re-ask, footer link that clears the record and reopens the banner, denied Consent Mode update, _ga deletion, ga-disable flag, salted IP hash), while Response A gives a generic backend design with no ga-disable flag or _ga deletion, no timestamp-based re-ask, and no clear-record footer behavior.
